notes:
Summary: Cerulean is evaluating Redwood Dedicated with Private control plane for latency-sensitive edge inference. Primary driver is predictable throughput & strict SLA for telco-grade service delivered to enterprise customers.

POC/Procurement context:
- Stage: procurement, heavy focus on contract SLA language, credits, and maintenance windows.
- POC ask: 2-week stress + 72-hour failover sim. acceptance criteria = throughput >= baseline, latency SLO met 95/99.

SLA negotiation specifics (customer wants):
- Target uptime: 99.99% for production endpoints (requesting 99.995% on critical paths for routing).
- Credit schedule requested: sliding credits starting at 5% for monthly availability (>= 99.9% and < 99.99%), 10% for <99.9%, escalated credits + termination right if <99.0% sustained for 3 months.
- Maintenance windows: prefer SAT-SUN 01:00-05:00 PT, no more than 2 hours of planned maintenance per month per region; require 72-hour advance notice for planned downtime.
- Support response times: P1 (service-down) 15 min initial response, P2 (degraded performance) 1 hour, P3 (non-critical) 8 business hours. On-call escalation path required, named SLA contacts.
- Penalty cap: customer proposing credits capped at 50% of monthly invoice and right to terminate after repeated breaches (legal pushing back).

Throughput & reserved GPU planning:
- Baseline reserved capacity requested: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (steady-state).
- Burst policy: allow autoscale to 12 GPUs for traffic spikes; guaranteed burst capacity of 4 GPUs for up to 6 hours/day.
- Throughput guarantee: target sustained throughput of ~1200 tokens/sec for p99 concurrent workload (chat medium prompts); sustained throughput SLA needed for planning.
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 120ms for sub-256-token chat messages; 99th <= 250ms; tail latency mitigation via KV-cache and batching.
- Model variants: want explicit routing/fallback clauses — if primary model unavailable, route to quantized variant with defined QoS and cost adjustments.
- Cache expectations: prefix and KV caching to be enabled; warm-up time and cache hit-rates to be included in POC report.

Security / compliance items in play:
- SOC2 attestation required before procurement sign-off; also SSO (SAML) and integration with existing KMS for key control.
- Data residency: EU regional residency required for 20% of traffic; need confirmation of region-level deployment and audit logging retention policy (13 months).

Quotes & customer color:
- CTO (L. Romero): "We can't afford >10 minutes of outage during business hours — our SLA has direct penalties from our downstream customers."
- Head of Infra: wants explicit capacity planning table in contract (mapping GPUs -> throughput -> latency).

POC success criteria / deliverables:
- Live throughput report showing steady-state tokens/sec and p95/p99 latency for 48h continuous run.
- Failover test to alternate region with <30s routing degradation.
- Security checklist signed: SAML, SOC2 docs, KMS integration validated.
- Drafted SLA with agreed credit schedule and maintenance windows.

Open questions for Redwood legal/ops:
- Will Redwood accept customer's proposed credit sliding scale and termination right? Legal to propose compromise (higher initial threshold, mediation clause).
- Can we commit to 72-hour advance notice for planned maintenance in contract language? Ops to confirm maintenance cadence.
- How will we document reserved GPU mapping to throughput (table required)? SE to run sizing matrix and include in annex.
